title: Redwood Optimize walkthrough - batching & KV cache cost model
summary: Redwood AE+SE walkthrough of Optimize recommendations focusing on batching and prefix/KV cache cost model for Mariner Payments. Discussed current infra, latency SLOs, data residency, security questions (SOC2/KMS/SAML), and next steps including benchmark POC and cost spreadsheet.
action_items: Alex Chen - send customized cost model spreadsheet and sample configs - 2026-12-08
Samir Patel - schedule benchmark slot and provide test harness (load script + prompt set) - 2026-12-10
Jordan Lee (Mariner) - share typical prompt distribution and 95th latency SLO target - 2026-12-09
next_steps: Run 2-day benchmark on Mariner test dataset (Redwood hosted/dedicated)
Security docs: SOC2 attestation + KMS integration guide
Follow-up call after benchmark to review numbers and rollout plan
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-06 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Riley Gomez (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Mariner CTO), Priya Nair (Mariner Head of ML), Marcus Holt (Infra Lead), Ava Ruiz (Product)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro we are from Redwood, I'm Alex AE and Samir and Riley are on the Optimize/infra side. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Jordan: good thanks, we are excited; been looking at your docs on batching and the kv cache notes.
[00:20] Priya: yeah we have a lot of chat-ish flows and also some long form summarization which is where we think caching might help.
[00:30] Samir: great; high level today we'll walk through batching patterns, prefix/KV cache, and then a simple cost model so you can see tradeoffs between latency and unit token cost. we'll also talk dedicated vs hosted routing and what to expect for a poc.
[01:05] Marcus: quick thing - our 95th percentile latency target is 350ms for auth flows; for summaries we allow up to 800ms.
[01:18] Riley: ok that's helpful, those numbers will guide batch windows and whether to enable aggressive caching.
[02:03] Alex: can you share current qps and prompt size dist?
[02:12] Jordan: right now about 120 rps peak, average 55, token distribution median 80 tokens, 95th around 700. most of the traffic is small queries for auth/decisioning and then a smaller set of long generative jobs.
[02:40] Priya: also, we need data residency in eu-west for EU customers and we need SSC2 - I mean SOC2 - and SSO via SAML.
[02:52] Samir: totally, we support region pinning and we have SOC2 docs and SAML SSO; we'll share the security pack.
[03:15] Alex: ok jumping into batching. the basic idea - continuous batching at the serving runtime aggregates requests to amortize GPU cost; you can tune target latency vs batch size. for interactive flows we often set small max batch windows (5-10ms) to keep latency low, for high throughput non-interactive we open to 30-50ms windows.
[03:50] Jordan: so if we go from 5ms to 30ms window what cost savings are typical?
[04:00] Samir: on throughput-heavy workloads it's common to see 20-35% token cost reduction due to higher occupancy. but it depends on seq length and model footprint; we include model-specific curves in the spreadsheet.
[04:30] Priya: but would that push our P95 over the 350ms?
[04:35] Riley: possibly if your median sequence is long and GPU queues up; that's why we recommend mixed policies: aggressive batching on background routes, conservative for auth. you can route by policy per endpoint.
[05:12] Alex: next, prefix / KV cache. prefix cache is great when requests share common prefixes - for example multi-turn chat or repeated API calls with similar histories. KV cache stores decoded key/value cache snapshots so you can fast-forward generation for common prefixes.
[05:40] Marcus: how much memory overhead does the KV cache add?
[05:45] Samir: depends on model and sequence length; for a 7B-ish model a cached prefix snapshot might be ~1-3MB per unique prefix; for Llama 2-13B it can be 3-8MB. we provide estimates. memory can be sharded and evicted via LRU policies.
[06:10] Jordan: we have many near-duplicate prompts in payments reconciliation, this sounds promising.
[06:20] Alex: right, two recommended patterns: 1) prefix caching for multi-turn and repeated phrasing; 2) KV snapshotting for long common prefixes where you can skip the forward pass. combine with batching to maximize throughput.
[06:40] Priya: ok cost model—walk us through an example.
[06:45] Samir: sure. example baseline: hosted without caching, avg token cost X. with prefix caching and medium batching we model 30% token compute reduction and small increase in mem ops cost. net savings ~22% in unit cost. with dedicated reserved capacity and optimized quantization you can add another 15% reduction but that requires commit.
[07:20] Alex: we'll share a spreadsheet with scenario rows: hosted small batch, hosted medium batch + prefix cache, dedicated reserved + kv cache + int8 quant, etc. you'll be able to plug in your qps and token dist to get monthly $ estimates.
[07:40] Jordan: can we see latency impact in that spreadsheet?
[07:44] Riley: yes can show P50/P95 estimates per scenario; they're model-driven estimates, best to validate with short benchmark.
[08:05] Marcus: about warmup and cache priming - how do we seed the prefix cache?
[08:12] Samir: two ways: proactive priming with a warm-up job (ingest top N prompts) or on-demand population via traffic. warm-up is recommended for critical flows. we can help run a priming job during poc.
[08:40] Priya: in terms of security - what about encryption of cached payloads and KMS integration?
[08:50] Alex: KV snapshots and cache blobs are encrypted at rest; KMS integration is supported for customer-managed keys. we'll attach the KMS guide.
[09:10] Jordan: perfect. another point - we use private deployment for sensitive EU customers. can your private option support the same optimize features?
[09:20] Riley: yes, the Optimize recommendations and runtime work similarly in both hosted and private, although quantization and autoscaling knobs are different when you're on-prem. some features like cross-tenant pooling are only in hosted.
[09:45] Marcus: what about rollout / canary? we need A/B test and rollback if quality dips after quant changes.
[09:52] Samir: we support canary rollouts per model version and automatic fallback to a higher fidelity variant on quality regressions. Redwood Optimize can hook into your eval sets and alert on regressions.
[10:15] Alex: let's jump into a rough POC plan. We propose 3 steps: 1) share cost model + config templates, 2) run 48-hour benchmark on your traffic sample (hosted + dedicated baseline), 3) review results and recommend configuration and rollout path.
[10:38] Priya: timeline wise we want results before the end of the quarter; that's about 3 weeks away.
[10:45] Alex: doable if we start this week. Samir will run the harness.
[10:55] Jordan: ok SLA/security questions for procurement - we'll need SOC2 attestation, an audit log sample, and SSO details.
[11:05] Alex: we'll send SOC2 and audit log guide, and SAML setup doc.
[11:18] Marcus: can you also include recommended instance sizing for dedicated? our infra budget needs a rough number.
[11:25] Samir: yes we'll include a sizing table using your qps and token dist.
[11:40] Ava: question on prompt engineering - do you see quality regressions when applying int8 quant to larger models?
[11:48] Riley: occasionally; that's why we recommend a phased roll out: run quality evals on held-out prompts and use automatic rollback thresholds. often quantization utility varies by model and task - chat vs summarization behave differently.
[12:20] Alex: quick demo — i will share my screen showing the cost spreadsheet and an example scenario.
[12:28] [screen share noise] Alex: here's a hosted baseline row: 1200k tokens/day, cost $Y baseline. row two: with prefix cache and mid batching you see token compute down 28% and net monthly savings $Z. note the memory overhead column; you'll probably want to cap per-prefix retention to control mem.
[13:30] Priya: can you show P95 numbers for the mid-batch cached scenario?
[13:35] Riley: P95 estimate 310ms for short flows, 650ms for long flows in that scenario — and that's within your stated targets.
[14:05] Jordan: curious about eviction behavior during spikes - if we have a big flash refund event will caching thrash?
[14:12] Samir: we use adaptive eviction; also you can pin important prefixes or reserve a hot-cache pool. for spikes we recommend burst capacity or fallback routing to a lower-batched path.
[14:45] Priya: is there built-in circuit breaker if latency degrades?
[14:50] Alex: yes, automatic fallback policies can route to a higher-capacity but higher-cost path or to an unbatched low-latency path. these are configurable per route.
[15:10] Jordan: any compliance gotchas for storing prefix snapshots?
[15:16] Samir: we avoid storing user PII in cache unless customers request and agree to controls; snapshots can be configured to redact or exclude sensitive fields. plus encryption at rest and access controls.
[15:40] Marcus: ok pricing asks - do you price caching differently?
[15:45] Alex: cache storage has a small monthly charge per GB for reserved, and for hosted we include a mem-op cost in the token pricing scenario; the spreadsheet breaks down compute vs storage vs network.
[16:05] Priya: can we run the benchmark on dedicated reserved, or only hosted?
[16:10] Riley: we can run both; for dedicated we'll simulate your target reserved config and show throughput/latency curves. it takes a little more setup (provisioning), but we can do a short run.
[16:30] Jordan: ok let's confirm the timeline and owners.
[16:35] Alex: recap: Alex will send cost spreadsheet + SOC2/SAML docs; Samir will provision harness and schedule the benchmark; Jordan will provide sample prompt set and SLO targets. we'll aim to start warm-up within 48 hours.
[16:50] Pria - sorry Priya: small note, we also want per-route token accounting exposed in your console for cost-splitting by product team.
[16:58] Riley: that's exposed in Redwood Console today, we can turn on role-based dashboards for your teams.
[17:10] Jordan: great. thanks everyone.
[17:15] Alex: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the spreadsheet.

End of transcript.
